newsitem.title: USA: USDA says monitoring Canadian wheat "very closely".
newsitem.headline: USDA says monitoring Canadian wheat "very closely".

text.p: The United States is concerned about the impact of Canadian wheat exports and is monitoring them "very closely," Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman said on Wednesday.
"I'm concerned about them," Glickman told reporters when asked about the current level of Canadian wheat exports into the United States. "They are being monitored very closely."
U.S. growers have become worried about competition from Canadian wheat exports.

Canadian and U.S. officials have previously projected wheat and barley shipments to U.S. buyers would be about 1.4 to 1.5 million tonnes in the year ending Sept. 12. That level would be roughly equal to a trade ceiling established in 1994 but which has since lapsed.
Glickman said no talks had been scheduled with the Canadian government to discuss current wheat export levels.
"I have some personal concerns that the levels of our (wheat) exports have not been going up in recent years and we're trying to find different strategies to help facilitate exports," Glickman said.
He said the strategies would include trade promotion and "the potential of using" the Export Enhancement Program, although adding that "I'm not advocating that right now."

"We are still year-in and year-out the most predictable supplier of wheat in the world," Glickman told reporters following a speech to an Asian-Pacific group at the USDA. "We intend to be major dominant forces in the world wheat market... We are going to look at all of our options."
